children: Higher gasoline costs are encouraging people to buy more fuel-efficient vehicles, and that will make for a tougher U.S. sales environment for General Motors (GM, Financials) and Ford Motor
, according to a projection from Cox Automotive.
Cox sees the two Detroit automakers suffering the most U.S. market-share losses of any major automakers in 2026.

The shift is significant since historically GM and Ford have depended on larger vehicles, notably highly profitable pickup trucks and SUVs. If customers become more concerned about fuel economy, sustained changes in consumer tastes could put pressure on that combination.

The shifting market also offers a chance for competitors like Toyota (TM), Hyundai, Tesla (TSLA) and Stellantis (STLA) as manufacturers fight for customers who are modifying their car choices to increased gasoline costs.
The challenge for GM and Ford is whether demand for their most profitable vehicles can hold up even as the larger U.S. market changes to more efficient models.
The next catalyst will be monthly U.S. sales data that should provide a stronger indication as to whether the market-share losses observed by Cox are accelerating.

title: GM and Ford Just Got a Troubling New Signal From U.S. Car Buyers
